correctness.rationale: For all a,b>=3 the graph distance matrix has 2 on all distinct same-side pairs and 1/3 on cross pairs according to deleted matching membership. Every same-side pair is distinguishable precisely when at most one unprotected vertex remains on its side; hence k+x<=1 and k+y<=1 are both necessary and sufficient. Disjoint k=0 and k=1 counting gives the all-set polynomial. A complete single-deletion classification gives every minimal-set case. The crown probability is exactly a zero-or-one binomial event, with the stated Poisson limit. A BFS distance implementation independently verified all 15,872 subsets in 41 cases, including 4,473 resolving and 979 inclusion-minimal sets. Smaller sides are explicitly excluded.

originality.rationale: The full metric-dimension scalar theorem for balanced matching deletion (Saputro et al. 2011, Theorem 1), generic parameterized algorithmic results (Galby et al. 2022), bipartite resolving bounds (Shahida–Sunitha 2020), and related different graph/metric variants were compared by mathematical implication. The connected-chain-graph resolving polynomial already covers t=0 and t=1 and those boundary formulas are not claimed as new. For t>=2, matching-deleted bicliques contain an induced 2K2, so that chain-graph result does not entail the new complete polynomial and inclusion-minimal transition. No other inspected statement covers those non-chain cases. Searches do not certify global novelty; unindexed overlap remains a material but presently nondecisive publication-priority risk.

value.rationale: A natural density interpolation from K_{a,b} through a partial deleted matching to the crown graph is classified at every resolving-set cardinality and every inclusion-minimal cardinality. The result determines an exact nontrivial if-and-only-if phase boundary 0<t<min(a,b) for non-well-dimensioned graphs, with complete multiplicities and a meaningful random-landmark failure window. This information is not inferred from any inspected scalar metric-dimension theorem.
